general.gpu_hint: Controls analysis and stacking by stage. Auto and Hybrid may restart a failed GPU stage on CPU after quality and resource checks. GPU only is strict: an eligible GPU-stage failure stops the job instead of silently falling back.

general.purity_hint: Controls the automatic limiters that cap what each slider does. Protected avoids halos, limb ringing and blown highlights. Pure lets the slider win, at the cost of those artefacts possibly returning.
general.purity_balanced_warning: Limiters at 50%: more effect per slider, with moderate risk of halos on high-contrast edges.
general.purity_pure_warning: No limiters: dark rings on the limb, background worms and blown highlights may return on a full Moon or solar disk.

common.interactive_hint: Interactive tutorial: use the highlighted control when it applies, or press Next and move at your own pace.

step0.title: Welcome to Zenith Astro Stacker!
step0.content: This is a general overview of how the software works. You can move with Next, and in guided workflows use highlighted controls when the tutorial asks for them.

step1.title: Import Video
step1.content: Start here by importing your SER or AVI files to process them individually.

step2.title: Batch Mode
step2.content: Process multiple videos automatically with the same configuration.

step3.title: Create Mosaic
step3.content: Join multiple lunar or solar panels into a single high-resolution image.

step4.title: Settings
step4.content: Adjust language and tutorial preferences here.

step5.title: Check for Updates
step5.content: Click here to search for new versions of the software and keep it up to date.

step0.title: Step 1: Import Video
step0.content: Start by selecting a .SER or .AVI video to process.

step1.title: Target Type
step1.content:
Choose the workflow language that best describes your capture.
Surface: Moon, Sun, or wide-detail scenes.
Planet / Lunar Phase: compact objects with a cleaner background.

step2.title: Step 2: Start Analysis
step2.content: Press this button now! to begin analyzing all frames. The system will evaluate the quality of each frame automatically.

step3.title: Preparing Analysis
step3.content: The system is starting the frame analysis. Please wait a moment while the data is processed.

step4.title: Step 3: Frame Selection
step4.content: Adjust the percentage of the best frames to stack. More frames = less noise, but includes lower quality frames.

step5.title: Step 4: Stacking Options
step5.content: Here you adjust Drizzle, Double-Pass Alignment, and Sharpening. Keep them conservative when you want a clean reference before fine post-processing.

step6.title: Step 5: Smart AP
step6.content: The Smart AP Generator creates the alignment mesh. Adjust AP Size and Threshold if you need finer points or more selective detection.

step7.title: Viewer: Source
step7.content: Before stacking, review the reference frame and alignment-point mesh here. This helps confirm that the system is tracking the right areas.

step8.title: Step 6: Start Stacking
step8.content: Once parameters are set and the source view looks right, press this button to begin stacking.

step9.title: Processing Details
step9.content: This card summarizes the stack: time, frames used, engine, AP points, throughput, and system details. Use it to validate that the process behaved as expected.

step10.title: Viewer: Result
step10.content: This is your stacked image. You can zoom and pan to inspect the details.

step11.title: Wavelets and Processing
step11.content: Adjust wavelets, deconvolution, color, and denoise from this card. Keep the Processed Result visible on the right so you can judge each change before continuing.

step12.title: Export Result
step12.content: Finally, save your processed image. You have options to export in PNG (8-bit) for general use or TIFF (16-bit) to preserve maximum quality.

step0.title: Batch Mode
step0.content: Use this workflow when you want to process several videos with the same calibration. First, select the folder that contains your captures.

step1.title: Batch Panel
step1.content: Here you will see the folder, the number of videos found, and the batch stages. This panel guides the workflow through final execution.

step2.title: Batch Target Type
step2.content: Choose whether the whole batch is Surface or Planet / Lunar Phase. This sets the analysis and alignment engine for every file.

step3.title: Batch Reference
step3.content: Load the first video to calibrate analysis, stacking, and post-processing. That setup becomes the template for the rest of the batch.

step4.title: Analyze Reference
step4.content: Run analysis on the reference video. The system measures quality, stability, and the data needed to repeat the workflow.

step5.title: Frame Selection
step5.content: Adjust the percentage of best frames. This value is used as the base for every video in the batch.

step6.title: Stacking Options
step6.content: Review Drizzle, Double-Pass Alignment, Normalize Colors, and Sharpening. These settings become the base recipe for the batch.

step7.title: Batch Smart AP
step7.content: Set AP Size and Threshold, then generate the Smart AP mesh. This helps the reference track the right detail before the recipe is repeated.

step8.title: Viewer: Source
step8.content: Review the reference and generated mesh here. Confirm that points cover useful areas before stacking.

step9.title: Stack Reference
step9.content: Stack the reference to validate the result before applying the same recipe to the full batch.

step10.title: Processing Details
step10.content: This card summarizes the reference stack: time, frames used, engine, AP points, throughput, and technical details.

step11.title: Post-Processing
step11.content: Adjust wavelets, deconvolution, color, and denoise on the reference while checking the Processed Result. These values will be replicated across every video.

step12.title: Batch Control
step12.content: Return to the batch panel to review completed stages and confirm the reference is ready as the template.

step13.title: Start Full Batch
step13.content: When the reference looks right, start the full batch. The system applies the validated configuration to the remaining files.

step14.title: Animation Editor
step14.content: When processing finishes, results move to the animation editor so you can review frames, reject bad ones, and export the final video.

step0.title: Mosaic Mode
step0.content: Use this workflow to join lunar or solar panels. You can work with videos that will be stacked first or with already processed images.

step1.title: Mosaic Sources
step1.content: Select the videos or images that will form the mosaic. Keep panels from the same session together to make stitching easier.

step2.title: Auto-Organize
step2.content: Press Auto-Organize so the system can place panels in the source viewer and you can review the initial layout.

step3.title: Source View
step3.content: Here you can inspect how the tiles were arranged before analysis, stacking, or final stitching.

step4.title: Global Analysis
step4.content: Analyze all panels to measure quality and prepare a consistent result. Wait for this to finish before continuing.

step5.title: Mosaic Process
step5.content: If you are working with videos, set the stacking percentage here and stack every tile before stitching.

step6.title: Guided Mode and Creation
step6.content: Create the final mosaic here. You can enable Guided Mode when you want your manual placement to have priority, but the recommended path is leaving it off so automatic stitching can find matches on its own. Press Create Mosaic and wait for it to finish.

step7.title: Step 6: Save or Process
step7.content: Mosaic completed! You can save as PNG/TIFF or send it to Wavelets for additional processing.

assistant.name: Intelligent Assistant

artifacts.summary_ringing: Relevant halos or overshoot were detected; use moderate correction and verify with A/B.
artifacts.summary_defects: Point defects dominate; use conservative denoise before increasing sharpness.
artifacts.summary_clear: No severe artifacts were found in the sample; keep adjustments gentle.
artifacts.apply_body: The measured correction will be applied reversibly so you can compare it with A/B.

control-help.title: Control help
control-help.message: I will take you back to the control and keep its contextual explanation.

batch-scan.title: Set the batch scope
batch-scan.message: Use this folder only when it contains one session; include subfolders when each capture is organized inside it.

batch-load.title: Prepare the batch reference
batch-load.message: {{itemCount}} videos detected. Tune one representative video and Zenith will reuse that traceable recipe.

batch-analyze.title: Analyze the reference
batch-analyze.message: The reference sets quality, mesh and percentage for the whole batch. Make sure it represents the session well.

batch-run.title: The batch recipe is ready
batch-run.message: Review the output folder and run it. Every video keeps traceability and will not be overwritten.

batch-complete.title: The batch is complete
batch-complete.message: {{completedItems}} of {{itemCount}} results are available. Review the sequence and open any master that needs individual finishing.

mosaic-load.title: Add the mosaic panels
mosaic-load.message: Use captures with compatible overlap and orientation. The assistant will continue through analysis, stacking and stitching.

mosaic-analyze.title: Analyze every panel
mosaic-analyze.message: Zenith measures quality and consistency before stacking to avoid seams with uneven detail.

mosaic-stack.title: Stack the panels
mosaic-stack.message: Confirm the suggested percentage and build a consistent master for every panel before composition.

mosaic-compose.title: Compose and inspect the seams
mosaic-compose.message: Order the panels, validate overlap and create the mosaic. Shared post-processing is available afterward.

mosaic-result.title: The mosaic is stitched
mosaic-result.message: Inspect the seams and open post-processing. History starts from the original mosaic.

deepsky-step.message_0: Add frames and let Zenith group exposure, filter and calibration signature.
deepsky-step.message_1: Review PSF, matches and warnings; incompatible data will not be mixed silently.
deepsky-step.message_2: Start with Auto or a profile and open advanced options only when expert control is needed.
deepsky-step.message_3: The plan is valid. Check the linear outputs and run the integration.
deepsky-step.message_3_blocked: The plan shows a material incompatibility. Open the review and correct it before continuing.

no-source.title: Load a source
no-source.message: Choose a video, sequence or result to begin.

histogram-unavailable.title: 16-bit diagnostics are missing
histogram-unavailable.message: Refresh the measurement before changing levels; this does not modify the image.

needs-analysis.title: Analyze before stacking
needs-analysis.message: Analysis detects quality, motion and the best reference frame.

ready-to-stack.title: Ready to stack
ready-to-stack.message: Review percentage, target and method, then start stacking.

object-finishing-start.title_surface: Choose a lunar or solar finish
object-finishing-start.message_surface: Lunar relief, full-phase and mineral recipes are available; creative recipes stay separate from scientific ones.
object-finishing-start.message_planet: Start with a natural recipe, then tune deconvolution, wavelets and color with A/B.

clipping.title: Protect tonal range
clipping.message: Measured clipping: shadows {{shadow}}% and highlights {{highlight}}%. I can neutralize aggressive levels and compensate the affected extreme.

ringing.title: Reduce halos before sharpening
ringing.message: Artifact analysis measured halos at {{ringing}}. Apply the measured recipe and verify it with A/B.

colour-fringe.title: Review RGB alignment
colour-fringe.message: Measured fringing is {{fringe}}. Zenith can estimate R and B again on the 16-bit master.

low-dynamic-range.title: The signal is compressed
low-dynamic-range.message: About 99.8% of useful signal occupies {{low}}–{{high}}. I can expand it with a safety margin.

dark-result.title: Midtones are very low
dark-result.message: The median is {{median}}%. A {{ev}} EV compensation brings it to a useful reading without moving black.

solar-mono-workflow.title: Is this a mono solar capture?
solar-mono-workflow.message: Useful signal occupies about {{range}}% of the range. If this is the Sun, I can build a conservative H-alpha derivative with curve, false color and noise protection.

solar-filaments.title: Filaments are still neutral
solar-filaments.message: The solar curve is active, but protected filament recovery is still zero. Measure it visually with A/B without altering the master.

tone-curve-opportunity.title: The tone curve is still linear
tone-curve-opportunity.message: I can create a gentle curve from the current histogram to separate shadows, midtones and highlights.

mono-color.title: Protected monochrome path
mono-color.message: RGB colorimetry and atmospheric alignment are locked. For solar data, Solar Lab can create false color without converting or replacing the mono master.

compare-ready.title: You can validate the adjustment
compare-ready.message: Enable A/B and choose Previous step or Original stack; both views preserve zoom and framing.

result-ready.title_continue: Continue one change at a time
result-ready.message_continue: History is active. Adjust one module, compare it and keep only the visible improvement.
result-ready.message_start: Recommended order: levels and curve, detail restoration, noise, then color.

deepsky.view_requires: The "{{view}}" view is only produced when stacking with {{engine}}. This master used a different engine: use Reintegrate and pick that method to produce it.
deepsky.spcc_seed_hint: The FITS header has no RA/Dec or scale. Enter the approximate field centre and your rig's pixel scale.
deepsky.guide_strict: Strict policy blocks on the first breach; you can continue in degraded mode (recorded)
deepsky.alert_silence_hint: Hide this warning for this session
deepsky.linker_hint: Link a specific batch to each night's lights, or skip flats/darks for that night. Untick a batch to exclude it entirely. Everything is recorded in the matrix and the recipe.
deepsky.manual_hint: Manual assignment is recorded in the decision matrix and the recipe; the batch choice is your responsibility.
deepsky.proceed_hint: Strict policy blocks on the first contract breach. You can continue in degraded mode: stacking proceeds, every concession is recorded, and the result is flagged as non-scientific where it applies.
deepsky.profile_auto_note: Measures your data (light count, filter, dithering, gradient, background) and sets the optimal recipe; every decision and its reason stay visible in the plan.
deepsky.repeat_integration_hint: Keep frames and registration; revisit only the integration recipe
deepsky.method_blocked_nonlinear: EIDR and NebulaFusion require linear scientific inputs (FITS/TIFF); check the plan warnings.
deepsky.dither_prediction_note: Pre-registration prediction from star offsets; stacking recomputes it with the real registration.
deepsky.pattern_hint: Dithering + robust rejection mitigate banding; check darks/bias from the same session.
deepsky.title: Deep-Sky Stacking
deepsky.hint: Pick your lights and (optional) calibration. Reference, star alignment, satellite rejection and stretch: automatic.
deepsky.step_assistant_0: Add lights; calibration frames are optional. Zenith groups compatible signatures and prevents silent mixing.
deepsky.step_assistant_1: Review grouping, PSF and calibration. Warnings explain exactly what to correct before integration.
deepsky.step_assistant_2: Auto is the recommended starting point. Open advanced controls only when your target needs them.
deepsky.step_assistant_ready: The plan is compatible. Confirm the linear outputs and run it when ready.
deepsky.step_assistant_blocked: Blockers remain. The guide takes you to the exact control that needs correction.
deepsky.step_assistant_empty: Add lights so I can prepare and validate the integration plan.
deepsky.data_intro: Add lights and calibration frames. Zenith groups geometry, Bayer pattern, filter, exposure, gain, binning and temperature.
deepsky.inspect_intro: Review grouping, applicable calibration, incompatibilities and warnings before choosing the recipe.
deepsky.preflight_empty: Add lights to prepare the plan.
deepsky.psf_pending: PSF inspection runs when you enter this step.
deepsky.recipe_intro: Choose a recommended profile. Open advanced options only when you need control over each stage.
deepsky.profile_fast_note: Bilinear, additive normalization and one sigma pass.
deepsky.profile_balanced_note: Lanczos-3, robust scaling and Winsorized rejection.
deepsky.profile_max_note: Winsorized rejection and local normalization; uses more RAM/CPU.
deepsky.multiband_enable: Process every filter in one multiband session
deepsky.multiband_summary: Zenith keeps each integration separate under one shared recipe.
deepsky.multiband_waiting: Shown when Zenith detects two or more spectral profiles.
deepsky.multiband_note_body: {{filters}}. Zenith will run {{count}} separate integrations in one session, extract their lines and keep a shared recipe.
deepsky.fixture_rejection_reason: FWHM and eccentricity are outside the robust range
deepsky.advanced_summary: Advanced options · registration, rejection, normalization, memory and engine
deepsky.review_intro: Confirm groups, effective method, CPU/GPU per stage and estimated resources. Fallbacks are shown before the run starts.
deepsky.footer_2: choose a profile or advanced options
deepsky.footer_add_lights: add lights to prepare the plan
deepsky.sessions_hint: Each night keeps its lights, signatures and calibration. ✓ is confirmed by Strict preflight; ? means candidate files only.
deepsky.dark_flats_header_detected: {{count}} identified from IMAGETYP plus FlatWizard context.
deepsky.scan_signature_note: Zenith will validate each signature before using it.
deepsky.done: Deep-sky stacked. View is auto-stretched; data stays linear for post-processing.
deepsky.method_hint_nf: NebulaFusion and EIDR are experimental and activate only when explicitly selected; Auto keeps the classic engine. NebulaFusion publishes VAR/NEFF/DQ maps alongside the master.
deepsky.cfa_direct_hint: Each photosite keeps its own color; requires CFA lights.
deepsky.split_hint: Saves R, G, B and a synthetic L as mono 16-bit TIFF to tweak per channel and recombine (LRGB/SHO).
deepsky.hoo_hint: Derived HOO view of the dual-band master: Ha→R, OIII→G and B (background neutralized). Only the VIEW changes — the linear float32 master (SCI/VAR/NEFF/DQ) stays intact; Reintegrate or switch views to return to the original RGB.
deepsky.spcc_hint: Photometric color calibration against Gaia DR3 (broadband OSC/RGB, needs internet). For narrowband/dual-band use HOO/SHO.
deepsky.no_base: No destination folder to export to.
deepsky.session_quality_hint: Measured linear masters and metrics, not the STF view.
deepsky.review_no_blockers: No blockers; the contract is ready.
deepsky.review_outputs_body: Linear master and reproducible recipe; SCI/VAR/NEFF/DQ when the plan is scientifically eligible.
deepsky.review_technical: View technical plan, signatures and fallbacks
deepsky.calibration_matrix_truncated: Showing 50 of {{count}}; the recipe preserves every decision.
deepsky.frame_open_hint: Click to view the stretched frame and its reason
deepsky.psf_inspection_hint: Click a row to view the stretched frame and its reason. Discard removes it from the plan and stack reversibly; the final decision is recomputed from the complete calibrated data.
deepsky.frame_reason_ok: No observations: metrics are within the batch
deepsky.viewer_stretch_hint: View stretch (STF). Does not modify the stacking data.
deepsky.viewer_balance_hint: Neutralizes the background per channel (removes the linear OSC green cast), view only.
deepsky.inspecting_frames: Measuring stars, PSF/FWHM, noise and eccentricity…
deepsky.reading_headers: Reading headers and preparing the plan…
deepsky.scan_folder_hint: Reads IMAGETYP; folders and names are safe fallbacks
deepsky.work_dir_choose_hint: Click to choose where caches, masters and exports are stored
deepsky.work_dir_change_hint: Click to change the working and output folder
deepsky.frame_groups_hint: Lights are required; calibration is optional and validated by signature.
deepsky.plan_scale_note: Darks from a different exposure were found. They will not be accepted or scaled unless the backend validates pedestal state, absence of amp glow, linearity, correlation, and residual.
deepsky.plan_dark_flat_note: Dark-flats do not match the flat exposure. Strict policy will block incompatible calibration.
deepsky.plan_candidate_note: ? = candidate by name/filter/exposure. Only the Strict preflight matrix confirms scientific compatibility.
deepsky.drag_hint: Drag a file to another category to reclassify it · ✕ to remove
deepsky.export_hint: Saved to your work folder (or next to your lights if none is set). The stretch uses the current mode/intensity.
deepsky.combine_desc: Assign one MONO stack per channel. They are star-registered to each other and combined. Luminance (L) is optional and adds detail/SNR while preserving color.
deepsky.combine_rgb: RGB / LRGB (true color · background neutralize + SCNR)
deepsky.combine_sho: SHO — Hubble (SII→R · Ha→G · OIII→B · no SCNR)
deepsky.combine_need: Assign at least channels R, G and B (or Ha/OIII).
deepsky.combine_done: Channels combined. Adjust the stretch in the bottom bar.
deepsky.auto_crop_note: At the end, the border frame with fewer overlapping frames (dithering/rotation) is cropped. Turn it off to keep the full framing, with noisier edges.
deepsky.local_weighting_note: Each sky region is stacked preferring the frames where THAT region came out sharpest (local seeing). Zenith exclusive: traditional stackers only weight whole frames.
deepsky.work_dir_hint: Next to the lights; choose another disk for caches, masters and exports
deepsky.work_dir_pick: Working & output folder (caches, masters and exports)
deepsky.advisor_reco_superres: Recommended scale: {{scale}} — super-resolution candidate once EIDR is available
deepsky.wbpp_hint: One row per night, filter and exposure. Pick the block of flats or darks you want to link to each group, or leave it on Auto and let the signature decide.
deepsky.scan_accumulates: You can scan more folders: they add to the previous ones. Use ✕ on a group to empty it.
